## Natural history notes

A small aquatic weevil characterized by its mottled brown-gray body, short snout, and compact oval shape that helps it blend into water hyacinth leaves and stems. In Florida, it is found in ponds, lakes, canals, marshes, ditches, and other slow-moving freshwater habitats where invasive water hyacinth grows. Adults feed on water hyacinth leaves and petioles, while the larvae tunnel into the petioles and crown; because it is host-specific and damages water hyacinth, it has been used as a biological control agent for this invasive aquatic plant.
